page: Microsoft Azure E32ps_v7 is a memory-optimized cloud server built on 64-bit ARM architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provisions 32 dedicated vCPUs paired with 256.0 GB of memory, establishing a consistent 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. This balance addresses workloads requiring heavy in-memory data retention without over-allocating core compute capacity. It contains zero integrated GPU accelerators, making it strictly dedicated to general CPU-based compute and memory processing tasks.

Storage configuration on the E32ps_v7 is entirely remote, as the instance includes no local or ephemeral drive space. Persistent data storage is managed through external Premium Storage volumes connected across the network infrastructure. The absence of local disk drives simplifies state management and node decommissioning, though disk I/O performance relies fully on attached network block volumes rather than high-speed local NVMe media.

Qualitatively, the combination of dedicated ARM execution cores and a high RAM density provides favorable operational efficiency relative to conventional x86 architectures, particularly for sustained enterprise deployments. The server is well suited for memory-intensive workloads, including large-scale relational database engines, in-memory caches such as Redis or Memcached, data warehousing ETL stages, and memory-bound enterprise applications.
description: Microsoft Azure E32ps_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Epsv7 series, powered by Microsoft Hyper-V. It features an arm64 processor architecture with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The server includes no integrated GPUs and provides no local ephemeral storage, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage for persistent data handling. The ARM-based architecture presents high hardware efficiency and density for large-scale deployments, reducing operational energy demands compared to legacy x86 alternatives while maintaining a substantial memory footprint. Lacking local NVMe disks, I/O operations are strictly bound by network-based volume performance. This configuration is tailored for memory-bound workloads that do not require low-latency scratch disks, such as distributed in-memory caching tiers, relational database engines, large analytical processing pipelines, enterprise resource planning backends, and high-concurrency memory-intensive application services.
